drafted_from: tool:keep-a-voice-edit's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep what the person changed in words an AI wrote for them, so their voice is learned from it", with {"before":"Same words.","after":"Same words."}. It runs tool:keep-a-voice-edit and answers {"edit":null}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes the words an AI wrote and the words the person changed them to, and gives back the row to keep (or none). The store is written by workflow:keep-how-someone-does-their-thing, not by this tool.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Keep what the person changed in words an AI wrote for them, so their voice is learned from it", and give it kind, subject_id, before (the AI's words), after (theirs) and before_by.
2. The AI calls tool:keep-a-voice-edit; when the words did not really change it answers edit null and keeps nothing.
3. When it answers an edit, the workflow writes keep at its edit_id through the person's own store and retires the older edits beyond keep_edits.
